problem.paragraph: If $$f$$ is a polynomial of degree $$4$$ and $$P_{4}(x)$$ is the fourth Taylor polynomial of $$f$$ at $$a$$ , then $$f(x) \neq P_{4}(x)$$ for at least one value of $$x$$ .
The function $$f(x) = 1 \slash (x - 2)$$ has a Taylor polynomial at $$a$$ for every value of $$a$$ except $$a = 2$$ .

Suppose $$f$$ is a polynomial of degree $$N$$ and $$R_{N}$$ is the remainder associated with $$P_{N}$$ , the $$N$$ th Taylor polynomial of $$f$$ at $$a$$ . Then $$R_{N}(x) = 0$$ for every value of $$x$$ .
Let $$P_{N}$$ denote the $$N$$ th Taylor polynomial of the function $$f(x) = e^{- x}$$ at $$a$$ . Then $$R_{N}(x) = f(x) - P_{N}(x) \neq 0$$ for all $$x \neq 0$$ .
